verses.1: And in the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he dreamed dreams. His dreams became terrifying, and his years became full of suffering.
verses.2: And the king said to call the Chaldeans, the Asmashim, the Mekashsim, and the Khasdim, so that they could tell the king his thoughts. So they came and stood before the king.
verses.3: And the king said to them, “I have a dream. My dreams have come true.”
verses.4: And the captives spoke to the king in Aramaic. They said, “We wish to serve you.”
verses.5: King Malcha replied, “You know nothing about me. My dreams and desires will be fulfilled. In your land, I will be honored.”
verses.6: And they were also blessed and honored. Their virtues were recognized by their ancestors. They received blessings from their ancestors.
verses.7: We will answer with gratitude, and we will say, “May the king who dreams of serving Him be granted success.”
verses.8: The king replied, “From where I stand, I know that you are a man of great wisdom. You can handle anything that comes your way.”
verses.9: May they not deceive me anymore. It’s clear that they are evil and corrupt. They want to say to me, “Before the time comes, let them be deceived.” But I know that their words are false; they will only deceive me.
verses.10: They answered, “No, before the king.” They said, “We are not people who can be controlled by any king or ruler. We refuse to submit to anyone’s commands.”
verses.11: And because of the king’s request, Yaqira and Aharon said, “Let them be honored before the king.” But the gods who ruled over them did not agree with this decision.
verses.12: Everyone who receives the kingdom of God will be blessed and rejoice. He will say, “May this kingdom be for all wise men.”
verses.13: And a law was established; and the wise men were killed. And in Daniel’s time, his friends also were killed.
verses.14: Beydian Daniel said, “Let them be punished and destroyed by the king who will bring about their downfall.”
verses.15: He replied and said to Arion: “How can the king know what religion was practiced in ancient times? He doesn’t even know anything about it. So, Arion answered to Daniyel.”
verses.16: And Daniel will be given one of the kings of that time. And he will be able to rule over those kings.
verses.17: Aden Daniel L’baytheh Azal and L’hananyah Mishael. And Azarya, his companion, also from L’tana Hoda.
verses.18: And may mercy be upon them from ancient times, O Lord. May they not be destroyed by the forces of darkness. And may they be united with the other wise men of Babylon.
verses.19: Adaiin for Daniel in the vision of Yeliyala Razah. Adaiin Daniel blessed her, O Elaia Shmayaya.
verses.20: Daniel replied, and said to Hawa: “Her name is ‘Elahah’. She is blessed from this world to the world to come. She is the wisdom and glory of those who worship her.”
verses.21: And he sets the times and days for kings to reign. He also chooses kings who are wise and capable of making decisions wisely.
verses.22: He knew everything about its depth and hidden secrets. He understood how it worked, along with all its mysteries.
verses.23: Go, O my God! Bless and honor me. May You, with Your wisdom and majesty, bless me. Now that You know me by Your eyes, from the words of the king, I know You too.
verses.24: Everyone who accepts Dana Daniel will be blessed by the king. He will be honored among the wise men of Babylon. And so, he said to them, “Do not honor me before the king and Pharaoh.”
verses.25: Eadain arioch behitbhalah haneil leDaniel kaddam malkha. And he said to her, “For forgetting the great ones among the children of Galaad, who are Jews from Israel, it is wrong for a king to do so.”
verses.26: King Malcha replied to Daniel, saying, “In your name, Beltshachar, I have made this dream. It is a vision for me to understand.”
verses.27: Daniyel answered first, and said, “Raza di-malkha shae’la la chakimin ashfin harutmin gazrin yakhlin le-hawaya le-malkha.”
verses.28: In my name, the divine one, I declare that I know everything. I know what it means to be king. My dreams and visions will come true while I sleep.
verses.29: You, king of the people, who lie down in your beds, remove what is harmful from around you. After all, you know what’s harmful.
verses.30: And I do not know through wisdom what is best for me among all the things that exist. Please tell me about the matters related to the laws of the Jews, so that my heart may understand them.
verses.31: You, king, have seen that it is possible to do so. And those shadows are nothing but illusions. They cannot truly be trusted. They will not be able to accept you.
verses.32: He took her head and made it into a beautiful ornament. It was made of gold and silver.
verses.33: His legs were covered with iron; his feet were also covered with iron.
verses.34: He watched as the stone was broken apart by his hands. It fell onto his feet, covered with brass and other metals.
verses.35: Bēdāyin dāku kahadā pārzlaḥāsphā nakhshā kāsfā vā dāhabā. Vā hāwō kē‘ur min irdēi-kayit, u nshā hīmūn ruḥā. Vā kullāt lā hisṭakhā lōn. Vā abnā ‘dī-machat lētalmā hāwāth lētur rāb. U məlāt kullāt ar’ā.
verses.37: You are the king, king of all kings. May your reign be prosperous and lasting. May God bless you.
verses.38: And in every place where human beings live, there is life. May the name of God be glorified in your hands and under your rule over all of them. You are the head of all those who live there.
verses.39: And in your place will rise a king. But before that, there will be chaos and destruction. And after that, there will be a king who will rule over everything.
verses.40: And four kings will rule over them, like a shield that protects everything it covers. Everything that comes under its protection is protected as well. And the shields of those who do evil will be broken and destroyed.
verses.41: And I saw their feet and their legs. They were covered with gold and silver. The king stood among them. All those who received gold were blessed. The gold was mixed with precious metals.
verses.42: And my feet will be covered with bronze, and they will be covered with iron from the edges of the kingdom. From there, it will become a fortress, and from there, it will become a citadel.
verses.43: And you see that the “parzela” is mixed with “hassaf tinah”. It’s mixed together with “anashah” and those who aren’t “hanah”. They’re mixed together, but the “parzela” isn’t mixed with “hassaf”.
verses.44: And in those days, my king will establish a kingdom that will last forever. Its reign will not end for any people. It will grow stronger and expand over all kingdoms. And it will endure forever.
verses.45: Everyone who receives the gift of vision must be careful not to let it escape from his hands. The metal ring must be tightly fastened, so that it won’t slip away. And one must also remember that God knows everything that will happen in the future.
verses.46: Bedarim Malkha Nebukadnezar fell upon Anphohi. And Ladaniel offered sacrifices and offerings as an offering of thanks. He said to Nasaka, “Lah.”
verses.47: King Malchai replied to Daniel, saying, “From the very beginning, this god has always been our god. He rules over kings and creates tears that you can see.”
verses.48: Eddin became king of Daniel. He was a great leader and ruler over all the lands of Babylon. He also had great authority over all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.49: And Danial was taken captive from his kingdom. He became a servant in the kingdom of Babylon, to serve there. Danial was in a difficult situation under the rule of the king.
